talk_track: I ran engineering at a defense SDVOSB for sixteen years and fielded a patented tactical app platform with operators in theater — then watched it die force-wide because no one senior inside the building championed it. Your open Deployment and Test Engineer role in Rome, NY says the job exists so that "the deployment, integration, and sustainment of Swoop technology, for mission critical customers, will usher in the advancement and reduction of time fielding these capabilities." That reads to me as a company whose constraint has moved off the OS itself and onto months-to-field — the same clock that just ran out on the $9.7M MDA "Swoop Operating System Demonstration and Test Report" vehicle on March 31 (HigherGov). A deployment engineer can compress the pipeline, but not the advocacy chain: operators who love SwoopOS don't create a program of record, a sponsor with a requirement does. Building that chain from the operator up is the work I do for defense startups, and a current TS/SCI means the classified half of it doesn't wait on access. What does months-to-field look like for the Rome work? — Barry Hess
